headline: Bitcoin clears $64,000 ahead of Wednesday's Fed rate decision
summary: Bitcoin pushed above $64,000 during Asian trading hours, pulling most of the top 20 assets higher as traders positioned ahead of a Federal Reserve decision due Wednesday. The Fed meeting is the day's real story — markets are split on whether the central bank will hold rates or hike, and that uncertainty is keeping the Fear & Greed index deep in fear territory at 29. Cardano led altcoin gains while NEAR Protocol slipped against the trend.

winners.name: Cardano
winners.catalyst: Cardano caught a bid alongside Bitcoin's move above $64,000, with altcoins broadly gaining as the larger-cap rally drew fresh capital into the market.

losers.name: NEAR Protocol
losers.catalyst: NEAR Protocol declined against the broader market trend, with traders pulling back from smaller-cap assets amid uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's upcoming rate decision.

whyItMoved:
Bitcoin crossed $64,000 during Asian trading hours, a level that has drawn attention as a near-term milestone, and the move lifted most of the top 20 assets. The immediate backdrop is Wednesday's Federal Reserve interest rate decision, which is dividing professional opinion sharply — hedge fund Citadel is positioned for a rate hike while many Bitcoin analysts expect the Fed to hold rates steady. That disagreement is visible in the Fear & Greed index sitting at 29, well into fear territory despite today's price gains; traders are moving cautiously rather than confidently.

Notably, the rally held even as South Korea's chip sector suffered a significant market crash — a reminder that crypto's correlation with traditional equity markets is not constant. Bitcoin's resilience in that context drew commentary from analysts tracking cross-market flows.

XRP was the strongest performer among the top 15, rising 2.8%, while Cardano led the broader altcoin field with a 4.7% gain. NEAR Protocol was the day's notable decliner, falling 4.3% as traders rotated away from smaller-cap assets ahead of the Fed announcement. The overall market cap sits at $2.28 trillion with Bitcoin holding 56.6% dominance, suggesting the rally is still concentrated in larger assets rather than spreading broadly into altcoins.
worthKnowing: Wednesday's Federal Reserve meeting is the week's central event for crypto markets — Citadel is betting on a rate hike while most Bitcoin analysts expect a hold, and the outcome will be known before Thursday's open.

A company behind an AI-driven trade that triggered $60 million in crypto liquidations has agreed to cover all losses, according to CoinDesk — an unusual outcome that may reduce some of the residual market uncertainty from that event.
Bitcoin's climb above $64,000 came despite a record crash in South Korea's chip market, which had no measurable spillover into crypto prices.
